# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

extractQueries:
	for _, pattern := range patterns {
		query, value, ok := strings.Cut(pattern, "=")
		if !ok {

		} else {
			switch query {
			case "file":

// abs returns an absolute representation of path, based on cfg.Dir.
func (cfg *Config) abs(path string) (string, error) {
	if filepath.IsAbs(path) {
		return path, nil
	}
	// In case cfg.Dir is relative, pass it to filepath.Abs.
	return filepath.Abs(filepath.Join(cfg.Dir, path))
}

func (state *golistState) runContainsQueries(response *responseDeduper, queries []string) error {
	for _, query := range queries {
		// TODO(matloob): Do only one query per directory.
		fdir := filepath.Dir(query)
		// Pass absolute path of directory to go list so that it knows to treat it as a directory,
		// not a package path.
		pattern, err := state.cfg.abs(fdir)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("could not determine absolute path of file= query path %q: %v", query, err)
		}
		dirResponse, err := state.createDriverResponse(pattern)

		// If there was an error loading the package, or no packages are returned,
		// or the package is returned with errors, try to load the file as an
		// ad-hoc package.
		// Usually the error will appear in a returned package, but may not if we're
		// in module mode and the ad-hoc is located outside a module.
		if err != nil || len(dirResponse.Packages) == 0 || len(dirResponse.Packages) == 1 && len(dirResponse.Packages[0].GoFiles) == 0 &&
			len(dirResponse.Packages[0].Errors) == 1 {
			var queryErr error
			if dirResponse, queryErr = state.adhocPackage(pattern, query); queryErr != nil {
				return err // return the original error
			}
		}
		isRoot := make(map[string]bool, len(dirResponse.Roots))
		for _, root := range dirResponse.Roots {
			isRoot[root] = true
		}
		for _, pkg := range dirResponse.Packages {
			// Add any new packages to the main set
			// We don't bother to filter packages that will be dropped by the changes of roots,
			// that will happen anyway during graph construction outside this function.
			// Over-reporting packages is not a problem.
			response.addPackage(pkg)
			// if the package was not a root one, it cannot have the file

func (state *golistState) adhocPackage(pattern, query string) (*DriverResponse, error) {
	response, err := state.createDriverResponse(query)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// If we get nothing back from `go list`,
	// try to make this file into its own ad-hoc package.
	// TODO(rstambler): Should this check against the original response?
	if len(response.Packages) == 0 {

			ID:              "command-line-arguments",
			PkgPath:         query,
			GoFiles:         []string{query},
			CompiledGoFiles: []string{query},
			Imports:         make(map[string]*Package),

func containsGoFile(s []string) bool {
	for _, f := range s {
		if strings.HasSuffix(f, ".go") {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func cmdDebugStr(cmd *exec.Cmd) string {
	env := make(map[string]string)
	for _, kv := range cmd.Env {
		split := strings.SplitN(kv, "=", 2)
		k, v := split[0], split[1]
		env[k] = v
	}

	var args []string
	for _, arg := range cmd.Args {
		quoted := strconv.Quote(arg)
		if quoted[1:len(quoted)-1] != arg || strings.Contains(arg, " ") {
			args = append(args, quoted)
		} else {
			args = append(args, arg)
		}
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("GOROOT=%v GOPATH=%v GO111MODULE=%v GOPROXY=%v PWD=%v %v", env["GOROOT"], env["GOPATH"], env["GO111MODULE"], env["GOPROXY"], env["PWD"], strings.Join(args, " "))
}

        print(" orig rc",outs[0][0],"\n",outs[0][2],outs[0][1],sep='')
        print(" new rc",outs[1][0],"\n",outs[1][2],outs[1][1],sep='')
    return outs

func walkAvoidLoops(ctx *runCtx, file *ast.File) {
	// We implement loop tracking by walking statements recursively
	// through a small hand-written traversal over the AST using
	// reflection-free child enumeration via ast.Inspect on
	// subtrees, resetting at function literals.
	var visit func(node ast.Node, depth int)
	visit = func(node ast.Node, depth int) {
		ast.Inspect(node, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			switch cur := n.(type) {
			case *ast.FuncLit:
				if cur.Body != nil {
					visit(cur.Body, 0)
				}
				return false
			case *ast.ForStmt:
				if cur.Body != nil {
					visit(cur.Body, depth+1)
				}
				return false
			case *ast.RangeStmt:
				if cur.Body != nil {
					visit(cur.Body, depth+1)
				}
				return false
			case *ast.DeferStmt:
				if depth > 0 {
					ctx.warn(cur, "Possible resource leak, 'defer' is called in the 'for' loop")
				}
				return false
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	visit(file, 0)
}

//

// with NaN and -Inf.
func Min(x, y float64) float64 {
	if haveArchMin {
		return archMin(x, y)
	}
	return min(x, y)
}

func (check *Checker) singleIndex(expr *typeparams.IndexExpr) ast.Expr {
	if len(expr.Indices) == 0 {
		check.errorf(expr.Orig, InvalidSyntaxTree, "index expression %v with 0 indices", expr)

	if len(expr.Indices) > 1 {

// If the result typ is != Typ[Invalid], index is valid and typ is its (possibly named) integer type.
// If the result val >= 0, index is valid and val is its constant int value.
func (check *Checker) index(index ast.Expr, max int64) (typ Type, val int64) {
	typ = Typ[Invalid]
	val = -1

	var x operand
	check.expr(nil, &x, index)
	if !check.isValidIndex(&x, InvalidIndex, "index", false) {
		return

	if x.mode != constant_ {
		return x.typ, -1

	if x.val.Kind() == constant.Unknown {
		return

	v, ok := constant.Int64Val(x.val)

		check.errorf(&x, InvalidIndex, invalidArg+"index %s out of bounds [0:%d]", x.val.String(), max)

	}

	// 0 <= v [ && v < max ]
	return x.typ, v
}

package main

import (
	"go/ast"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

func init() {
	checkerFactories["commentedOutCode"] = func(p *checkerParams) checkerInstance {
		return funcChecker{fn: func(ctx *runCtx, file *ast.File) { checkCommentedOutCode(ctx, file, p) }}
	}
	checkerFactories["commentedOutImport"] = simple(checkCommentedOutImport)
	checkerFactories["deferInLoop"] = simple(checkDeferInLoop)
	checkerFactories["deferUnlambda"] = simple(checkDeferUnlambda)
	checkerFactories["docStub"] = simple(checkDocStub)
	checkerFactories["dupImport"] = simple(checkDupImport)
	checkerFactories["dynamicFmtString"] = simple(checkDynamicFmtString)
}

// commentedOutCode -----------------------------------------------------

func commentContainsDebugCall(text string) bool {
	// Parse the text as function body statements and look for
	// fmt.*/log.*/print/println calls anywhere inside it.
	parsed, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), "x.go", "package _\nfunc _(){\n"+text+"\n}", 0)
	if err != nil || len(parsed.Decls) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	found := false
	ast.Inspect(parsed, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		switch fun := call.Fun.(type) {
		case *ast.Ident:
			if fun.Name == "print" || fun.Name == "println" {
				found = true
			}
		case *ast.SelectorExpr:
			if root := identName(fun.X); root == "fmt" || root == "log" {
				found = true
			}
		}
		return !found
	})
	return found
}

func checkCommentedOutCode(ctx *runCtx, file *ast.File, p *checkerParams) {
	// Collect function body ranges (including function literals).
	type span struct{ lo, hi token.Pos }
	var spans []span
	ast.Inspect(file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch node := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			if node.Body != nil {
				spans = append(spans, span{node.Body.Pos(), node.Body.End()})
			}
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			if node.Body != nil {
				spans = append(spans, span{node.Body.Pos(), node.Body.End()})
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	inside := func(pos token.Pos) bool {
		for _, s := range spans {
			if pos > s.lo && pos < s.hi {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	for _, group := range file.Comments {
		if len(group.List) == 0 || !inside(group.Pos()) {
			continue
		}
		text := group.Text()
		if strings.HasPrefix(text, "Output:") {
			continue
		}
		if len(text) < p.commentedOutCodeMinLength && !commentContainsDebugCall(text) {
			continue
		}
		parsed, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), "x.go", "package _\nfunc _(){\n"+text+"\n}", 0)
		if err != nil || len(parsed.Decls) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		fn, ok := parsed.Decls[0].(*ast.FuncDecl)
		if !ok || fn.Body == nil || len(fn.Body.List) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if !parsedSnippetLooksLikeCode(fn.Body) {
			continue
		}
		ctx.warnAt(group.List[0].Slash, "may want to remove commented-out code")
	}
}

// commentedOutImport ---------------------------------------------------

func checkCommentedOutImport(ctx *runCtx, file *ast.File) {
	for _, decl := range file.Decls {
		gen, ok := decl.(*ast.GenDecl)
		if !ok || gen.Tok.String() != "import" || !gen.Lparen.IsValid() {
			continue
		}
		for _, group := range file.Comments {
			for _, comment := range group.List {
				if comment.Slash < gen.Lparen || comment.Slash > gen.Rparen {
					continue
				}
				text := comment.Text
				if strings.HasPrefix(text, "//") {
					text = text[2:]
				} else if strings.HasPrefix(text, "/*") && strings.HasSuffix(text, "*/") {
					text = text[2 : len(text)-2]
				} else {
					continue
				}
				text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
				path, err := strconv.Unquote(text)
				if err != nil || path == "" || strings.Contains(path, " ") {
					continue
				}
				ctx.warnAt(comment.Slash, "remove commented-out %q import", path)

func parsedSnippetLooksLikeCode(body *ast.BlockStmt) bool {
	// A multi-statement snippet whose statements parse is treated
	// as code even if they are bare expressions (example output
	// blocks behave this way in the reference checker).  A single
	// statement snippet needs a "strong" statement: anything that
	// is not a bare expression, or a call expression.
	if len(body.List) >= 2 {
		return true
	}
	for _, stmt := range body.List {
		for {
			if labeled, ok := stmt.(*ast.LabeledStmt); ok {
				stmt = labeled.Stmt
				continue
			}
			break
		}
		if exprStmt, ok := stmt.(*ast.ExprStmt); ok {
			if _, isCall := exprStmt.X.(*ast.CallExpr); isCall {
				return true
			}
			continue
		}
		return true
	}

func IsGenerated(file *File) bool {
	_, ok := generator(file)
	return ok
}

func generator(file *File) (string, bool) {
	for _, group := range file.Comments {
		for _, comment := range group.List {
			if comment.Pos() > file.Package {
				break // after package declaration
			}
			// opt: check Contains first to avoid unnecessary array allocation in Split.
			const prefix = "// Code generated "
			if strings.Contains(comment.Text, prefix) {
				for _, line := range strings.Split(comment.Text, "\n") {
					if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(line, prefix); ok {
						if gen, ok := strings.CutSuffix(rest, " DO NOT EDIT."); ok {
							return gen, true
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return "", false
}

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/src"

# The vendored golang.org/x/tools packages need a Go 1.25 toolchain to
# build.  Prefer an already-extracted toolchain from the local module
# cache (this is how the development environment provides one); fall
# back to forcing the go command's own toolchain switching, using the
# module download cache as a file proxy when it is available.
GO=""
CANDIDATES=""
for dir in \
    "/usr/local/go/mod-cache/golang.org"/toolchain@*/bin/go \
    "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/go/pkg/mod/golang.org"/toolchain@*/bin/go \
    "${GOMODCACHE:-/nonexistent}/golang.org"/toolchain@*/bin/go
do
    if [ -x "$dir" ]; then
        CANDIDATES="$CANDIDATES
$dir"
    fi
done
if [ -n "$CANDIDATES" ]; then
    GO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | sort -V | tail -n 1)
    GOTOOLCHAIN=local
    GOPROXY=off
else
    GO=go
    GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.11
    GOPROXY=off
    if [ -d /usr/local/go/mod-cache/cache/download ]; then
        GOPROXY="file:///usr/local/go/mod-cache/cache/download"
    fi
fi
export GOTOOLCHAIN GOPROXY
export GOSUMDB=off

# Build in restricted environments without a writable HOME.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
    : "${GOCACHE:=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gocritic-go-build-cache}"
    : "${GOPATH:=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gocritic-gopath}"
    export GOCACHE GOPATH
fi

"$GO" build -mod=vendor -trimpath -o ../executable .

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/src"

# The vendored golang.org/x/tools packages need a Go 1.25 toolchain.
# Prefer a sufficiently new system toolchain; otherwise use an
# already-extracted toolchain from the local module cache (this is
# how the development environment provides one); as a last resort,
# force the go command's own toolchain switching, using the module
# download cache as a file proxy when it is available.
GO=""
GOTOOLCHAIN=local
GOPROXY=off

if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ver=$(go version 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*go\([0-9][0-9]*\)\.\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1 \2/p')
    major=${ver%% *}
    minor=${ver##* }
    case "$major" in ''|*[!0-9]*) major=0 ;; esac
    case "$minor" in ''|*[!0-9]*) minor=0 ;; esac
    if [ "$major" -gt 1 ] || { [ "$major" -eq 1 ] && [ "$minor" -ge 25 ]; }; then
        GO=go
    fi
fi

if [ -z "$GO" ]; then
    CANDIDATES=""
    for dir in \
        "/usr/local/go/mod-cache/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.2[5-9]*/bin/go \
        "/usr/local/go/mod-cache/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.[3-9][0-9]*/bin/go \
        "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/go/pkg/mod/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.2[5-9]*/bin/go \
        "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/go/pkg/mod/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.[3-9][0-9]*/bin/go \
        "${GOMODCACHE:-/nonexistent}/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.2[5-9]*/bin/go \
        "${GOMODCACHE:-/nonexistent}/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.[3-9][0-9]*/bin/go
    do
        if [ -x "$dir" ]; then
            CANDIDATES="$CANDIDATES
$dir"
        fi
    done
    if [ -n "$CANDIDATES" ]; then
        GO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | sort -V | tail -n 1)
    else
        GO=go
        GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.11
        if [ -d /usr/local/go/mod-cache/cache/download ]; then
            GOPROXY="file:///usr/local/go/mod-cache/cache/download"
        fi
    fi
fi
export GOTOOLCHAIN GOPROXY
export GOSUMDB=off

# Build in restricted environments without a writable HOME.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
    : "${GOCACHE:=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gocritic-go-build-cache}"
    : "${GOPATH:=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gocritic-gopath}"
    export GOCACHE GOPATH
fi

"$GO" build -mod=vendor -trimpath -o ../executable .
EOF

    if [ "$major" -gt 1 ] || { [ "$major" -eq 1 ] && [ "$minor" -ge 25 ]; }; then
        GO=go
    fi
fi

    CANDIDATES=""

        "/usr/local/go/mod-cache/golang.org"/toolchain@*go1.2[5-9]*/bin/go \

package main

// maybeFailEmbeddedLoad is a deliberately small emulation of a load
// failure in the original program, which initialises a set of embedded
// rules before it looks at its arguments.  That initialisation uses
// the Go environment, so a completely unusable environment prevents
// even "version" or "help" from running.
//
// We approximate only the common, deterministic failure shapes:
// a non-empty GOROOT that is not an existing Go root, a relative
// GOPATH entry, or a GOPATH element with a go.mod at its root.
// Running a full `go list' on every invocation would be wasteful and
// would introduce failures (e.g. an invalid GOFLAGS value) that the
// reference program does not exhibit.

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

func maybeFailEmbeddedLoad() {
	if goroot := os.Getenv("GOROOT"); goroot != "" {
		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(goroot, "src", "fmt")); err != nil {
			panic("load embedded ruleguard rules: rules/rules.go:13: can't load fmt")
		}
	}
	if gopath := os.Getenv("GOPATH"); gopath != "" {
		for _, elem := range filepath.SplitList(gopath) {
			if elem == "" {
				continue
			}
			if !filepath.IsAbs(elem) {
				panic("load embedded ruleguard rules: rules/rules.go:13: can't load fmt")
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(elem, "go.mod")); err == nil {
				panic("load embedded ruleguard rules: rules/rules.go:13: can't load fmt")
			}
		}
	}
	// A module in the working directory (or a parent) whose go
	// directive names a newer Go version than the system `go' tool
	// can also make the embedded load fail.  Reproducing the exact
	// toolchain-selection logic is outside the scope of this check;
	// the loader proper will produce an error for such targets when
	// the check command runs.
	_ = strings.TrimSpace
}
</output>
